hook: Terry Sejnowski earned a BS in physics from Case Western Reserve University and a PhD in physics from Princeton University, followed by postdoctoral work in biology at Princeton and in neurobiology at Harvard Medical School. In 1985 he co-authored A Learning Algorithm for Boltzmann Machines with David Ackley and Geoffrey Hinton, introducing a stochastic learning method for neural networks. Working with Charles Rosenberg, he then built NETtalk, a neural network that learned to convert written English text into speech sounds, published in 1987 in Complex Systems and widely cited as an early demonstration that distributed neural networks could learn a complex cognitive task from examples. In 1988 he moved to the Salk Institute for Biological Studies, where he now holds the Francis Crick Chair and directs the Computational Neurobiology Laboratory, with a joint appointment at the University of California, San Diego. He founded the journal Neural Computation in 1989 and has served as its editor-in-chief since, and in 2018 he co-authored the book The Deep Learning Revolution. He was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2010 and has since received the Gruber Neuroscience Prize and the Brain Prize.

quick_facts: Professor and holder of the Francis Crick Chair at the Salk Institute for Biological Studies
Co-created NETtalk with Charles Rosenberg, an early neural network that learned to convert written English text into speech, published in 1987
Co-authored the 1985 paper introducing the Boltzmann machine learning algorithm with David Ackley and Geoffrey Hinton
Founded the journal Neural Computation in 1989 and has served as its editor-in-chief since
Elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2010
Co-authored the 2018 book The Deep Learning Revolution, published by MIT Press

achievements.title: NETtalk (1987)
achievements.impact: Built with Charles Rosenberg, NETtalk was one of the first neural networks to learn a complex cognitive task end to end, converting written text into phonemes for speech, and became a widely cited demonstration that distributed neural networks could learn structured behavior from data.

achievements.title: Boltzmann machine learning algorithm (1985)
achievements.impact: Co-developed with David Ackley and Geoffrey Hinton, this stochastic learning algorithm for neural networks became a foundational technique in the later development of deep learning.

achievements.title: Founding editor-in-chief, Neural Computation
achievements.impact: Launched and has edited the journal Neural Computation since 1989, giving computational neuroscience and neural network research a dedicated peer-reviewed home.

achievements.title: National Academy of Sciences and Brain Prize recognition
achievements.impact: Elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2010 and later awarded the Gruber Neuroscience Prize and the Brain Prize, recognizing decades of work bridging neuroscience and machine learning.
